clue.text: PM gets round part of Ireland

parts.note: Theresa May was a British Prime Minister (PM)
a round shape looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A prime minister travels around a region of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PM' is not a time of day here but a Prime Minister, Theresa May.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county in the west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: House with crazy exterior is let-down

indicators.note: the crazy word forms the outside wall, with the house sitting within it

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A house with an odd-looking outside proves a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior' tells you the crazy word wraps around the house abbreviation; 'let-down' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an anticlimax, a ludicrous drop from the lofty to the trivial.

clue.text: Woman offering half-truth

indicators.note: half of the word for truth is kept, its first four of eight letters

parts.note: veracity means truthfulness

explanation.surface: A woman tells only half the truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-truth' reads as a single idea but splits: take half of VERACITY, its front half VERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a female first name, so any woman so named fits the clue's generic 'Woman'.

clue.text: Performer in political party introduced by the German

indicators.note: the party sits inside the German article

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'
the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress party

explanation.surface: An entertainer joins a political party, sponsored by a German figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German' means the German word for 'the'; 'introduced by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer is one kind of stage performer.

clue.text: Wild boar (honest!) living among the trees

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the animal run riot into a new order

parts.note: honest in the sense of genuine, real

explanation.surface: A speaker swears a wild boar was really found in the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges BOAR to ARBO; the exclamation 'honest!' gives REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal describes animals that inhabit trees, such as squirrels and monkeys.

clue.text: Woman from the past in an Anglican church leading to tension

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England, the Anglican church
stress and tension are synonyms

explanation.surface: A woman of history in an Anglican church feels the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestress is a female forebear, someone from whom a person descends.

clue.text: Dispute by river somewhere in France

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river sits beside the dispute

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
to dispute is to argue

explanation.surface: A quarrel by a riverbank somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camargue is the Rhone delta region of southern France, famous for its white horses.

clue.text: Detective writer — one who knows about plots, it's said?

indicators.note: it's said marks a word heard rather than written

parts.note: a gardener knows about garden plots

explanation.surface: A crime writer is one who knows how to plot a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' looks like story plots but means patches of ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Erle Stanley Gardner wrote the Perry Mason detective novels.

clue.text: Excellent band broadcasting

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; written with the numeral read as I
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A superb band goes out on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (top quality) is written AI, the 1 standing as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Airing a programme is transmitting it, so the two terms are synonyms.

clue.text: Sort of test taken by that female who has given birth?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one who has given birth', a noun

indicators.note: the test is followed by the female, as if she takes it

parts.note: the MOT is the UK's annual roadworthiness test for vehicles
her refers to a female person

explanation.surface: A woman takes some kind of test.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is Britain's annual vehicle safety check. The definition borrows 'female' from the wordplay, so the clue is semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who has borne a child is that child's parent, so the description fits.

clue.text: A new job (not exciting one) daughter secured

parts.note: a chore is a tedious task

explanation.surface: A daughter lands a new, dull job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured' looks like part of the story of landing the job but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat anchored is held firmly in place, fastened.

clue.text: Tense? Things will never get better!

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense, as in 'I have eaten'
a cry that the current moment is ideal and cannot be improved

explanation.surface: Someone, uneasy, sighs that life will never improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an emotional state but is a grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical tense formed with have plus a past participle; read literally, the here and now being flawless.

clue.text: A victor, one involved in act of annulment

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters get tangled up together

explanation.surface: A winner takes part in an act that cancels something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A VICTOR plus ONE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A revocation is the official withdrawal or cancelling of a decree or licence.

clue.text: Live in squalid conditions as American soldier in hole

indicators.note: the soldier is placed within the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
GI is a term for a US soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier lives rough in a foxhole.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to live in a dirty, messy way, like a pig in a sty.

clue.text: A very old wife making one swear

explanation.surface: An elderly wife makes someone take an oath.
explanation.definitionFit: To avow is to declare or affirm solemnly.

clue.text: Arms tired, having carried piano on

indicators.note: the tired word holds the other pieces within it, as a carrier holds a load

parts.note: weary means tired
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's arms ache after lugging a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' looks like limbs but means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Weaponry is a collective term for weapons, which are also called arms.

clue.text: Just fine

definitions.meaning: just meaning fair and morally correct

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both morally proper and correct or acceptable.

clue.text: Disquiet ultimately about a delinquent youth given indulgence

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth rebel

explanation.surface: A troublesome youngster is spoiled, causing unease.
explanation.walkthrough: A TED (Teddy boy) was a 1950s British rebellious youth in Edwardian-style clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be treated is to be given a special pleasure or indulgence.

clue.text: Untruth provided by female willingly

parts.note: a lie is an untruth

explanation.surface: A woman tells a falsehood without hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Lief is an archaic adverb meaning gladly, as in 'I'd as lief stay'.

clue.text: Lecturer as host, awfully sweet

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A lecturer acting as host is terribly nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like an adjective about the lecturer but is a noun, a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte russe is a dessert of sponge fingers around a cream filling.

clue.text: Characters with questionable identity in Dutch city

indicators.note: the letters belong to the words that follow, spanning their join

explanation.surface: People with dubious identities turn up in a city in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people but means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Leiden is a university city in the Netherlands, in South Holland.

clue.text: Cheap meat for a 'hearty' meal?

parts.note: offal such as heart, liver and kidneys, the inner organs of a deer once baked into a pie

explanation.walkthrough: 'hearty' is literal: the meat includes the heart. Umble pie gives the phrase 'humble pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbles are the edible offal of a deer, once regarded as fare for the lower orders.

clue.text: I act with Tory somehow to expose this cruelty

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: Collaborating with a Conservative lays bare a wicked deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I ACT plus TORY; 'with' and 'to expose this' link.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an act of extreme cruelty or wickedness.

clue.text: Vegetables in start of summer month shooting up

indicators.note: in a down entry, shooting up means the letters run from bottom to top
start of picks the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: May is a month

explanation.surface: Vegetables sprout at the beginning of a summer month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting up' reverses SMAY in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Yams are starchy tubers eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: African country entertaining graduate in Caribbean territory

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the country holds the graduate inside

parts.note: Togo is a country in West Africa
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: An African nation hosts a graduate on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, part of Trinidad and Tobago.

clue.text: Energetic person in game, top lady

parts.note: Go is a board game
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A lively person in a game is the leading woman.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is crossword shorthand for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A goer is someone lively and full of drive.

clue.text: Part of the meal lacking refinement reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly marks a word heard as speech, not seen

parts.note: coarse means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: A dish is served without any finesse.
explanation.definitionFit: A meal is served in stages such as starter, main and dessert, each one a separate serving.

clue.text: Tot restricted by grown-ups, little boy exasperated

indicators.note: the tot sits hemmed in by the grown-ups

parts.note: men are grown-ups
to tot up is to add
Ed is a short form of the boy's name Edward

explanation.surface: A toddler, held back by adults, and a small boy grow irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a child but is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Maddened means made very angry, which is close to exasperated.
